title: Font, icons, menus, file-op progress
summary: The text engine is the strongest piece of 8088 engineering in this part of the kernel. font_run_x decides everything that belongs to a run once: the y test, both inks, the row base, the cell count, the trailing span and the plane grouping. It draws row-major from a pre-walked glyph-pointer table, so each cell row costs one store on mono and on VGA subset pairs, and unaligned runs cost n-1 plain stores plus two edge columns. Two systemic ideas have no period equivalent. The menu bar is a cell-diffed composition (menu_bcell is the record of what is on the glass). The file-progress widget is armed from the disk choke points and torn down only by gfx_unlock, so no caller can leave it up. The defects found are latent rather than live. fpg_bare banks the clip count but not the dock's hole, as every other bank site in the tree does. font_ink has a 14-byte VGA/gfx_mono1 arm that cannot be reached, and SPEC 11.96.17.1 still describes it as working. font_run leaves [gfx_color] differently depending on the path taken, and its header says otherwise. The menu layout measures package strings without a bound. OSAPI_FONT_GLYPHS can race the extended desktop's seam cut. The largest weakness is prose: about 45% of these files is comment, much of it 'it used to' history. Verification confirmed 32 of the 33 statements the reviewer found that no longer describe the code (in headers, SPEC and the SDK), and found three more, for 38 edits in all. Worthwhile rethinks are small and additive: kernel-synthesised BOLD in font_run, which retires the last structural reason for transparent text; real separator and check-mark item markers; and moving the once-per-run VGA prologue into the .vga rung.

strengths.title: font_run_x's run model
strengths.why: Everything that belongs to a run is decided once. The per-cell-row work is lodsw/xchg/add/mov/and/xor/stosb, with a +8-biased glyph-pointer table so the row counter's inc is the loop test. This is the right shape for any 'many cells, one pen' primitive on an 8088.

strengths.title: ROM font read in place, chosen and copied by measurement
strengths.why: FONT_PICK times the candidates with the PIT. The 760 bytes are copied into a pinned top-down heap claim only on a machine whose ROM is more than 25% slower than RAM, and the same macro re-asks at resume. Nothing is resident on machines that do not need the copy.

strengths.title: The menu bar is one composition, and composing it is the diff
strengths.why: menu_bcell is both the composition buffer and the record of what is on the glass. The padding is the erase, and a minute rollover redraws one glyph. menu_bput advances even when it drops a cell, which removed a livelock class by construction.

strengths.title: Save-under claimed per drop, sized from the rect, with a correct fallback
strengths.why: The claim is purgeable and movable. A refused or purged claim degrades to a damage-rect repaint, and the bdirty disarm around that repaint shows the XOR-highlight interaction was understood rather than patched.

strengths.title: MENU_DIS prefix and two labels over one db
strengths.why: Greying an item costs one byte and no structure: the live label is the tail of the greyed one. This is cheaper than the Mac's per-menu enable mask and needs no API.

strengths.title: The progress widget belongs to the freeze, armed at the choke points
strengths.why: dsk_xfer and drv_fs_call arm it, and gfx_unlock is its only teardown, so no bracket can be forgotten and no early return can leave it up. FPG_WARM stops a one-sector probe from flashing it on and off. None of DOS, Windows 3.x, OS/2 1.x or System 6 had a system-owned disk progress indicator.

strengths.title: Data and adjacency checked at assembly time
strengths.why: IREC/IRUN/IHALF/IEND turn a miscounted icon run stream into a build error. The %if adjacency guards (font_rn_fg/bg, xm/bm, ico_c1/c2, menu_bdirty/bovr, menu_seg/dseg) cost no bytes and fire on the edit that would break a one-word store.

strengths.title: One-shot icon pens are spent on refusal too
strengths.why: ico_c1/c2 are reset on the refused path as well as the drawn one, which is the case nobody tests.

strengths.title: menu_hover reads the pointer once under cli
strengths.why: It closes a torn-read race that was measured launching the wrong item 4 times in 320.

strengths.title: ascw.inc treats ASSOC.DAT as hostile
strengths.why: It checks the size against 64KB and the buffer, the magic, both counts against the caps, and the counts against the bytes actually read. It takes header fields only if the bytes reached them, treats an I/O error as different from 'no file', and reads the volume it writes about.

findings.title: fpg_bare banks [wm_clip_n] but not [gfx_hole]
findings.detail: fpg_bare zeroes the clip count, runs the painter, and restores the count. On a DOCK_OPT kernel, CLIPQ is gfx_clip_query: with wm_clip_n = 0 and the hidden dock's strip open, it tail-jumps to gfx_hole_arm, which re-seeds wm_clip_tab with the desktop minus the strip. fpg_bare then restores the caller's fragment count over the hole's table. The caller's next primitive in the same hold clips against the wrong region and can paint over windows above it. Every other bank site in the tree saves both words. toast_now also goes through fpg_bare.
evidence: kernel/vga12.inc:6638-6644 gfx_clip_run banks gfx_hole, comment names this exact hazard
findings.recommendation: Under %ifdef DOCK_OPT, push word [gfx_hole] / and word [gfx_hole],0 before the painter call and pop word [gfx_hole] after it, inside fpg_bare itself so that all callers are covered. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE. It needs a handler that draws through a region after file I/O in the same hold while the strip is open.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: fpg_bare (fprog.inc:161-170) banks only [wm_clip_n]; with it 0 and [gfx_hole] set, CLIPQ -> gfx_clip_query (vga12.inc:463-468) -> dkx_gfx_hole_arm (dockmod.inc:1542-1562) calls dkk_wm_clip_seed, overwriting wm_clip_tab, and fpg_bare then pops the caller's old count over the hole's table. menu_drop (menu.inc:1929-1935) and dkx_paint bank both words. Banking the hole is safe: the widget is in the bar's rows, never under the bottom strip. +13 checks out (push mem 4, and mem,imm8 5, pop mem 4). Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE. Live only with a region armed, the hidden dock open and file I/O in the same hold.

findings.title: font_ink's VGA early-out and [gfx_mono1] test are unreachable
findings.detail: font_ink has one caller, font_char_bb, which font_char reaches only on a 1bpp display (vid_mono != 0, or vid_planes < 4 under VID_EXT, which vid_depth_set keeps in step with mono). So mov al,[vid_mono] / or al,[gfx_mono1] / jz .vga never jumps, and .vga is dead. That is 14 bytes plus about 40 clocks per glyph on every mono string drawn by kern_big (~1.2% of a cell). SPEC 11.96.17.1 and vga12.inc still credit this test with behaviour that exists on no path.
evidence: kernel/font.inc:603-610 font_char only calls font_char_bb on 1bpp
findings.recommendation: Delete the three-instruction test and .vga on GFX_VGA builds, and re-balance the parity pad after it (t_hotpar). Correct SPEC 11.96.17.1 and vga12.inc:31 (see doc mismatches).
findings.verify_note: Only caller is font.inc:789 in font_char_bb; font_char reaches it only when vid_mono=1 (GFX_VGA) or vid_planes<4 (VID_EXT), and vid_depth_set writes mono/planes as one word: 1/1, 0/4, or 0/vx_bpp with vx_bpp 8 or 16. So `jz .vga` never jumps. 14 bytes = mov al,[m] 3 + or al,[m] 4 + jz 2 + mov [m],al 3 + jmp short 2. An even deletion, so parity holds; the comments at font.inc:952-962 claiming the OR serves 11.96.17.1 go with the code.

findings.title: font_run_x leaves [gfx_color] path-dependent and the contract is silent
findings.detail: The fast paths (.rm/.rmp/.rmu/.planar) never write the pen. .whole leaves it at the foreground. font_run_scell leaves it at the background for a refused cell. The header claims 'left at the run's foreground on a drawn run'. os88api.inc's OSAPI_FONT_RUN and SPEC 6.1 do not mention the pen. A package that draws with its pen after FONT_RUN gets different colours depending on adapter, theme and clip state.
findings.recommendation: Document that the pen is undefined after the call (in the SDK and SPEC 6.1), at zero bytes. Alternatively, bank AL at entry and restore it at .out (+8 bytes) if a clean contract is preferred.
findings.verify_note: Only font.inc:1954/1960 (.whole) and 2235/2272 (font_run_scell) store [gfx_color]; the mono, planar and unaligned row passes read font_rn_fg/bg only. The header's 'foreground on a drawn run' is false for every single-pass run. Doc fixes below make it UNDEFINED; whether to restore instead is the owner's call.

findings.title: OSAPI_FONT_GLYPHS can return the seam cut's borrowed table
findings.detail: On a SEAMCUT kernel, font_ch_seam points [font_seg]:[font_base] at LOW_SEG:font_seam_a minus a bias for one font_char call, under the gfx lock. osapi_font_glyphs takes no lock and reads the same pair, so a worker pre-empting the UI task mid-seam gets garbage glyphs. An app that copies the font before an FSX bracket would then keep the wrong font.
findings.recommendation: Keep a canonical pair for the API, written only by font_init, hbm_wake 4a and the kern_mega pool move. Alternatively, give the seam its own pair for font_char to load. The other option is to document the window in the slot row.
findings.verify_note: font_ch_seam (font.inc:448-458) rewrites both words for one font_char call and osapi_font_glyphs (kernel.asm:6627-6632) reads them with no lock; a pre-empting worker can also catch the pair torn between the two stores. SEAMCUT kernel only, and only while a seam cell is being drawn: low.

findings.title: Menu layout measures package strings with an unbounded font_width_x
findings.detail: font_width_x is 8 x len mod 64K. menu_widest measures each item with it and then clamps. An item of 8,192 or more non-NUL bytes wraps to a narrow rect, and therefore a narrow save-under, while menu_trunc still letters 24 cells. That leaves permanent garbage outside the rect, which is exactly what menu_trunc's header says it prevents. menu_relayout also places the first app menu after the full AM_NAME width, while the name cell shows a 24-glyph copy: names of 25-60 characters leave a gap, and a wrapping name overlaps.
evidence: kernel/menu.inc:570 vs 719 two different name widths
findings.recommendation: Bound the measure at MENU_MAXCH+1 (menu_trunc's repne scasb already does this) in menu_widest. Take the name width from menu_abstr+MENU_ABPFX_LEN after building it.
findings.verify_note: font_width_x is 8*len mod 64K (font.inc:2542-2557) and menu_widest (menu.inc:2427-2460) measures with it before clamping, so a NUL-less run of about 8,190+ bytes wraps to a narrow width. menu_trunc still letters MENU_MAXCH cells. That needs hostile or broken package strings: low. The name-width gap was not exercised: the full-width measure (menu.inc:570) against the menu_abstr copy (719) was read, not run.

findings.title: fprog's one-word-store adjacencies are only half asserted
findings.detail: fpg_finish's xchg ax,[fpg_on] and KHP_FPG's cmp word [fpg_on],0 need fpg_warm to follow fpg_on on every kernel, but the %if guarding this sits inside %ifdef FPG_PARK (kern_big only). The three stores that empty the trough state in one word (fpg_pat plus fpg_px's low byte) have no %if at all, only prose.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the fpg_warm guard out of the %ifdef and add %if fpg_px - fpg_pat != 1.
findings.verify_note: The %if (fpg_warm - fpg_on) != 1 at fprog.inc:1340-1344 is inside %ifdef FPG_PARK, but the xchg ax,[fpg_on] at 1228 runs on every kernel. fpg_pat/fpg_px adjacency is prose only; the %error at fprog.inc:110 guards px's high byte, not adjacency.

findings.title: font_run_x's once-per-run VGA prologue is resident on mono machines
findings.detail: MOVABLE-COLD-PLAN kept font_char's per-cell VGA writer in .text, rightly. font_run_x's .planar prologue plus its VESA door is 144 bytes by build/kernel.map (0x3E65..0x3EF5), and fnt_rn_edge's VGA arm is about 43 more (0x3F78..0x3FA3). Both run once per RUN, ahead of a ~4,300-cycle prologue, and both are dead on CGA/Hercules/MDA. The .vga rung's entry jump would cost about 15 clocks per run.
findings.recommendation: Move .planar/.vxp0 and fnt_rn_edge's VGA arm into .vga, with a tests/vgarefs.txt row guarded by the [vid_planes]/[vid_mono] test font_run_x already makes. KERN_BUDGET is measured on VGA, so the budget machine pays the small plus. Owner's call.
findings.bytes_est: ~-185 resident on mono kern_big machines, ~+10 on VGA/EGA (KERN_BUDGET)
findings.verify_note: The .planar span is right (map 0x3E65..0x3EF5 = 144). fnt_rn_edge's VGA arm is 0x3F78..0x3FA3, about 43 bytes, not ~25, so the mono saving is ~-185. A .vga move puts a jump on VGA's per-run path and adds to KERN_BUDGET, which is measured on VGA. Not queued in KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: [vid_popmax] is a constant held in a memory word
findings.detail: vid_popmax dw MENU_POPMAX has never been written since vid_apply stopped computing it. Its only reader, menu_setup, can use immediates.
findings.recommendation: Use cmp ax, MENU_POPMAX / mov ax, MENU_POPMAX and delete the cell.
findings.verify_note: Readers are menu.inc:1764/1766 only, besides comments and a C comment in apps/c64/c64menu.c. cmp ax,[m] 4 -> cmp ax,imm8 3; mov ax,[m] 3 -> mov ax,imm16 3; the dw goes: -3.

findings.title: VGA ico_pass keeps its per-word column bookkeeping in memory
findings.detail: Per source word, the pass does add word [ico_col],2, dec word [ico_wleft], and up to three cmp word [ico_col],imm. That is about 90 clocks a word, roughly 4.8 ms per 32x32 desktop icon on an XT with a VGA (the owner's 5150 with a PVGA1A). PREDICTED. The 1bpp twin moved the same state into DL/DH; the VGA pass cannot, because DX is the GC port. The VGA arm also lacks the fully-off-right early-out that ico_core_bb has.
findings.recommendation: Test once per icon whether col0+2*ww+2 <= ROW_BYTES and take a compare-free copy of .word (KHP_ICONWORD's idea, applied to the planar arm). The same test gives the off-right early-out.
findings.verify_note: ico_pass (icons.inc:592-655) keeps ico_col/ico_wleft in memory with three memory compares per word, and has no off-right early-out (ico_core_bb has one at 557-560). The clock figure is PREDICTED, as the reviewer says.

findings.title: ico_pass_bb makes a near call per framebuffer byte on shifted icons
findings.detail: There are three calls to ico_bbop_byte per word, each a call, a memory compare and a ret: about 55 clocks a byte. KHP_ICONWORD covers only shift 0 and is off pending LOG O5.
findings.recommendation: Price hoisting the op (two loop copies, as font_char_bb's .srow/.crow do) alongside row 15 when O5 is decided.
findings.listed_as: LAST-DROP-PERF.md row 15 (KHP_ICONWORD) covers the aligned half only
findings.verify_note: Three `call ico_bbop_byte` per word (icons.inc:771/786/795); LAST-DROP-PERF.md:602 row 15 is KHP_ICONWORD, gated on LOG O5.

findings.title: An empty volume keeps a stale ASSOC.DAT
findings.detail: When no package was placed, asw_close returns CF=1 and ascw_flush_x takes .same (success, nothing written). A volume whose packages were all removed keeps an old cache that names rows and associations for packages that are gone, even after a full-mode (installer) flush.
findings.recommendation: When an old file exists (asw_dclus >= 2) and the build is empty, write a valid 16-byte header with both counts 0 instead. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE; impact depends on how asc_use treats rows whose packages are missing.
findings.verify_note: asw_close .none returns CF=1 when ASC_NAPP - nb + nf = 0 (ascw.inc:976-979), and .built's `jc .same` writes nothing (153-154). The old file stands. Impact is PLAUSIBLE: asc_use's handling of rows for missing packages was not traced. FORMAT.DRV code, 0 resident.

findings.title: menu_drop and fpg_paint fill a ground, then letter over it
findings.detail: menu_drop fills the whole rect and then runs font_run_x over every item, so each text cell is written twice. fpg_paint fills the bed under the icon, frame and trough. Doing it exactly once with the available primitives would take MORE primitive calls (pad strips per item), and redraws are priced by calls. The clean answer is composition through the band, which has been a knob since SPEC 5.9.6.
findings.recommendation: Do not hand-fix this. Revisit only if BAND returns as a shipped feature.

findings.title: Two parity nops under complementary %ifdefs are one unconditional nop
findings.detail: %ifdef KERN_SMALL nop / %ifndef KERN_SMALL nop emits exactly one byte on every build, with two different stated reasons.
findings.recommendation: Collapse it to one nop carrying both reasons, or let text-2's edit re-derive it.
findings.verify_note: font.inc:1009-1017: `%ifdef KERN_SMALL nop` + `%ifndef KERN_SMALL nop` = one nop on every build.

findings.title: Routine headers carry history, and the history goes stale
findings.detail: Comment-only lines are 1,065 of font.inc's 2,793 lines, 1,288 of menu.inc's 2,721 and 811 of fprog.inc's 1,388, before counting the paragraph-long trailing comments. The mismatches found share one shape: the original contract line stands while a later pass appends a new paragraph about the change (font_char's whole-char clip, font_str_x's five callers, font_run_cell's '.slow', font_ink's planes, SAVE_SEG, MENU_SAVE_KB).
findings.recommendation: Adopt a convention, not a gate: headers state only the current in/out/clobbers/invariants. 'It used to' paragraphs move to the SPEC section or the pass's report, leaving a one-line pointer. Apply it file by file as each is next touched.
findings.verify_note: Counts reproduced with grep -c '^ *;': 1065/2793, 1288/2721, 811/1388. Of the 33 mismatches the reviewer listed, 32 held.

findings.title: Kernel-synthesised BOLD in font_run
findings.detail: Overstrike is now the only structural reason a text pixel is written twice (SPEC 6.6.2 case 6: Word, Texpad, Frotz x2, cword). STIKMENU.DRV already synthesises bold as row | row>>1, which stays inside the cell on the ROM 8x8 set. A one-shot run style plus a bold copy of the row loop would make bold one pass and retire case 6 along with its registry rows.
findings.recommendation: Add an additive one-shot style cell (like OSAPI_ICON_PEN) and a bold row loop in font_run_x on kern_big. kern_small can keep the plain loop.
findings.prior_art: QuickDraw's bold is a 1-pixel smear done by the text engine, and Windows GDI emboldens raster fonts the same way; in both, applications never double-strike.
findings.verify_note: SPEC 6.6.2 case 6 (overstrike) is as quoted, and STIKMENU.DRV's stm_text has STY_BOLD (stikmenu.inc:157, 1387-1432). The byte estimate is the reviewer's and was not re-derived. It adds an API cell, so it needs an abilock --update.

findings.title: Real separator and check-mark item markers
findings.detail: Separators are MENU_DIS strings of hand-counted dashes, sized to the widest item when written, so a wider item added later makes the rule short (the kernel has two such strings; isotron, pixel and realdmg have their own). MENU_DIS doubles as a radio mark, which reads as 'disabled'. Proposed: MENU_SEP draws one gfx_hline across the interior over the already-filled ground, and MENU_CHK puts a mark in the existing 8px left margin and stays selectable. menu_item_dis remains one compare.
findings.recommendation: Add MENU_SEP=2 and MENU_CHK=3 as prefix bytes alongside the SDK change; old kernels would draw MENU_SEP as a selectable blank.
findings.bytes_est: +~12 menu_drop, -17 kern_big menu_s_msep; net ~-5, plus package strings
findings.prior_art: Mac '(-' meta and CheckItem; Windows MF_SEPARATOR/MF_CHECKED; Intuition CHECKIT.
findings.verify_note: The two kernel separator strings are menu.inc:2523/2529 (and files.inc:2611/2613 fm_s_fsep, which the reviewer did not count). A 17-dash string is 19 bytes, and a MENU_SEP,0 string is 2, so the saving is -17, not -19 (corrected in bytes_est).

findings.title: The icon API is 16 px wide because the stage shares ico_ibuf with the desk band
findings.detail: ico_ibuf (256 bytes) could hold a 32x32 body, but ico_band occupies its top 136 bytes while a desktop cell composes, and OSAPI_ICON_DRAW is called inside that compose (the Wire's driver). A 32-px plain kind would need the stage moved out of the band.
findings.recommendation: Record only, so the limit is not 'fixed' into a band overrun. A 32-px kind costs +136 .bss.

findings.title: font_char's VGA writer multiplies y by 80 for every glyph
findings.detail: mov ax,ROW_BYTES / mul dx costs about 125 clocks per VGA glyph. The row table stops at 348 rows, and the 480-row table was refused after being measured. A shift-and-add y*80 saves about 45 clocks (~2% of a VGA cell) for about +13 resident bytes.
findings.recommendation: Not recommended. Recorded with the numbers so nobody re-derives it.

findings.title: No keyboard path into a menu
findings.detail: The keyboard mouse steps a dropped menu item by item (menu_kbnav), but nothing opens the bar from the keyboard. Windows used F10/Alt plus mnemonics; the Mac showed Cmd-key equivalents. A real model would map a key to opening cell N, arrows walk cells and items, and Enter returns menu_track's (cell, item) pair.
findings.recommendation: Record only. It is about 150-250 .cold bytes and outside the 'no huge growth' brief.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x Alt/F10 and accelerator tables; Mac Menu Manager Cmd-key equivalents; Intuition COMMSEQ.

doc_fixes.old_text:
; Clipping is whole-char: if any part of the 8x8 cell would leave the screen
; the glyph is skipped entirely (acceptable v1 behavior per SPEC.md 6) - and,
; while a background task's clip region is armed, if any part of the cell
; would leave THAT (SPEC.md 11.3). A glyph is one shape or none; the region
; is the only thing here that could produce half of one, and half an 8x8
; glyph is unreadable anyway.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; Clipping: a cell that would leave the SCREEN is skipped entirely (on a
; SEAMCUT kernel a cell a display seam crosses is cut there instead, SPEC.md
; 39.14.11). Against an armed clip region the cell is cut to the ROWS
; wm_clip_rows allows (SPEC.md 11.3.2) and, on kern_big, to the columns
; [wm_clip_cm] allows (11.3.4); a cell no fragment reaches draws nothing.
doc_fixes.why: font_char's CLIPQ arm calls wm_clip_rows (font.inc:548-570) and the row loops AND [wm_clip_cm] on KERN_BIG; font_ch_spill cuts at a seam

doc_fixes.old_text:
Clipping is **whole-cell**: a
glyph whose 8x8 cell would cross a screen edge is skipped entirely, and so
is one whose cell is not wholly inside a single fragment of an armed clip
region (§11.3) — a glyph is one shape or none, and half an 8x8 glyph is
unreadable.
doc_fixes.new_text:
A
glyph whose 8x8 cell would cross a screen edge is skipped entirely (a
display seam cuts it instead, §39.14.11). Against an armed clip region the
cell is cut by ROWS (§11.3.2) and, on `kern_big`, by COLUMNS too (§11.3.4),
so a cell an edge crosses draws the part on its side and one no fragment
reaches draws nothing.
doc_fixes.why: font_char asks wm_clip_rows, not wm_clip_test (font.inc:548-570), and masks columns with [wm_clip_cm] on KERN_BIG

applies the same shifted row masks to every
plane the adapter has (or/and-not per the `[gfx_color]` plane bit — at 1bpp
there is one plane and one bit, and `font_ink` rounds
doc_fixes.new_text:
applies the same shifted row masks to the
one 1bpp plane (or/and-not per the ink bit — `font_ink` rounds
doc_fixes.why: font_char_bb's plane loop is gone: it writes [vid_rseg] once (font.inc:770-785)

doc_fixes.old_text:
A hibernated image
carries the pointer and resumes only on the machine that wrote it, whose ROM
the image's own IVT already names (§87.3).
doc_fixes.new_text:
A hibernated image
carries the pointer, and the resume asks the reading machine again
(`hbm_wake` step 4a, §6.0.1).
doc_fixes.why: hbm_wake 4a re-runs FONT_PICK and refills a heap copy or replaces the ROM pointer (hiber.inc:5062-5100; SPEC 6.0.1 'The resume re-asks')

doc_fixes.old_text:
There is no RAM
; copy: the 768 bytes of .lowbss the table and its blank cell were are not
; resident on any machine.
doc_fixes.new_text:
There is no RESIDENT
; copy: the 768 bytes of .lowbss the table and its blank cell were are gone
; from every machine, and only one whose ROM font_init times more than a
; quarter slower than RAM copies the 760 into a 1KB MEM_K_FONT heap claim
; (SPEC.md 6.0.1).
doc_fixes.why: font_init copies FONT_BYTES into a MEM_K_FONT claim when the timed ROM is >1.25x RAM (font.inc:360-395)

doc_fixes.old_text:
; The same shifted-row masks as the VRAM path, applied to all four planes
; in software: the [gfx_color] plane bit picks or (set bits) or and-not
; (clear bits).
doc_fixes.new_text:

; 1bpp framebuffer's one plane: font_ink's reduced ink picks or (set bits)
; or and-not (clear bits).
doc_fixes.why: one write target, mov ds,[vid_rseg], no plane loop (font.inc:770-800); the ink is font_ink's 00/FF

doc_fixes.old_text:
; font_ink - internal: font_char_bb's per-plane colour register
;
; The glyph loop tests bit 0 of CH once per plane and shifts, so on VGA the
; colour index goes in untouched. On mono there is one plane and one bit to
; give it: gfx_ink's black or white.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; font_ink - internal: font_char_bb's ink register
;
; Its one caller is font_char_bb, which font_char reaches only on a 1bpp
; display, so there is one plane and one bit to give the glyph loop's

doc_fixes.old_text:
`font_ink` clears `[font_dith]` on the VGA path, so a greyed caption is a
checkerboard of black and white on Hercules and CGA and **solid colour 8** on
a VGA. An application cannot fix that from outside: `font_ink` is the
kernel's.
doc_fixes.new_text:
only the 1bpp renderer stipples (`font_ink`, whose one caller is
`font_char_bb`), so a greyed caption is a
checkerboard of black and white on Hercules and CGA and **solid colour 8** on
a VGA. An application cannot fix that from outside: the renderer is the
kernel's.
doc_fixes.why: font_ink is reached only from font_char_bb, on 1bpp (font.inc:603-610, 789); a VGA cell goes to font_char's .vram writer

doc_fixes.old_text:
So `font_ink` takes its mono path when `[vid_mono]` is set **or** the window
being drawn has declared two colours. That path reduces the ink to 00h or FFh
and sets `[font_dith]`, which is the checkerboard. Nothing new renders; an
existing path is reached from one more place.
doc_fixes.new_text:
`font_ink` tests `[gfx_mono1]` beside `[vid_mono]` for this, but its one
caller is the 1bpp `font_char_bb`, so on a VGA the test is never reached and
the declaration changes nothing there. What holds a VGA to the claim is
`font_run`'s planar prologue and `gfx_pen_dis`, below.
doc_fixes.why: font_ink's or al,[gfx_mono1] (font.inc:949-951) runs only when vid_mono=1; [gfx_mono1] is honoured at font.inc:1866 and vga12.inc:5019

doc_fixes.old_text:
different: §6.1's opaque renderer calls `font_ink` explicitly on **every**
adapter, and computes its own checkerboard without asking `[vid_mono]`.
doc_fixes.new_text:
different: §6.1's opaque renderer reduces the inks itself — inline in its
mono prologue, and from `[gfx_mono1]` and `[gfx_dis]` in its planar one —
and computes its own checkerboard without asking `[vid_mono]`.
doc_fixes.why: font_run_x has no call font_ink; it reduces inline (font.inc:1326-1350) and in .plset (1866-1900)

doc_fixes.old_text:

                                ; reducing the ink to 00h/FFh, which the glyph
                                ; loop turns into colour 0 and 15 across all
                                ; four planes, and stippling a disabled one
                                ; instead of leaving it solid CDGRAY.
doc_fixes.new_text:
font_run's planar prologue stipples a
                                ; disabled run instead of leaving it solid
                                ; CDGRAY, and gfx_pen_dis rounds the pen to
                                ; black (font_ink, the 1bpp renderer's, never
                                ; sees a VGA).
doc_fixes.why: the readers of [gfx_mono1] are font.inc:1866 (.plset) and vga12.inc:5019 (gfx_pen_dis); font_ink's test is reached only on 1bpp
